source_text:
Homilia i in sanctum pascha (homilia 3) (e cod. Sinaitico gr. 492)
Τοῦ μακαρίου Ἡσυχίου, πρεσβυτέρου Ἱεροσολύμων, εἰς τὸ ἅγιον πάσχα
1 Φαιδρὸς ὁ οὐρανὸς τῇ τῶν ἄστρων χορείᾳ καταλαμπόμε νος, φαιδρότερα δὲ
τὰ σύμπαντα ἑωσφόρου ἀνατέλλοντος, ἀλλ' ἡ παροῦσα τῆς νυκτὸς κατάστασις οὐ
τοσοῦτον ἄστροις καταυ γάζεται ὁπόσον νῦν ἀγάλλεται τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν
νε νικηκότος· «Θαρσεῖτε» γάρ, φησίν, «ἐγὼ νενίκηκα τὸν κό σμον»· θεοῦ δὲ
νικήσαντος τὸν ἀόρατον πολέμιον, εἰκότως καὶ αὐτοὶ τὴν κατὰ δαιμόνων νίκην
ἀποισόμεθα. Παραμείνωμεν τοί νυν τῷ σωτηριώδει σταυρῷ, ἵνα τὰς πρώτας ἀπαρχὰς
τῶν Ἰησοῦ δώρων ἀπενεγκώμεθα. Τὴν ἱερὰν ταύτην νύκτα δᾳ δουχίαις ἱεραῖς
πανηγυρίσωμεν, μέλος ἔνθεον ἐγείροντες καὶ ὕ μνον οὐράνιον ἐξᾴδοντες. «Ὁ τῆς
δικαιοσύνης ἥλιος», ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, καὶ τὴν παροῦσαν ἡμέραν τῷ
κύκλῳ τῆς οἰκουμένης κατεφώτισεν, διὰ σταυροῦ ἀνέτειλεν, τοὺς πιστοὺς διέσωσεν.
2 Μή τις τοίνυν ἀπιστείτω τοῖς τοῦ σταυροῦ συμβόλοις, ἀλλὰ τὸ μακάριον
καὶ τρισμακάριον ξύλον τοῦ σταυροῦ προσκυνείτω, καὶ τοῖς τοῦ σταυροῦ συμβόλοις
τοῦ θύρας οὐρανοῦ ἡμῖν ἀνοί ξαντος. Οὐκέτι «καίουσι λύχνον καὶ ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον
τιθέασιν», μόδιον δέ φημι τὸν Νόμον, «ἀλλ' ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν», λύχνον δὲ τὸν Λόγον·
ὑπὸ τὸν Νόμον δὲ ἐτύγχανεν καὶ ἐκρύπτετο τοῖς ἀπίστοις ὁ Λόγος ὡς ὑπὸ τὸν
μόδιον· ὅτε δὲ ἦλθεν ἐπὶ σταυροῦ καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν ἐτέθη, τότε τῷ τῆς οἰκουμένης
thought_title: The Easter Night and the Cross as Lampstand
orientation: Hesychius of Jerusalem opens his Easter homily by contrasting the natural brightness of the heavens with the surpassing joy of this night because Christ has conquered the world and the invisible enemy; he urges the congregation to cling to the saving cross and worship the wood of the cross as the lampstand on which the Word now shines to the whole world.
pass_a_gloss: The heaven is bright, being illuminated by the chorus of the stars. But all things are brighter at the rising of the dawn-bringer. But the present condition of the night is not so much illuminated by stars as it now exults in our God and Savior having conquered. For "Take courage," he says, "I have conquered the world." And God having conquered the invisible enemy, fittingly we also will carry off the victory over demons. Let us remain therefore by the saving cross, so that we may offer the first-fruits of the gifts of Jesus. Let us celebrate this holy night with holy torches, raising an inspired melody and singing a heavenly hymn. "The Sun of Righteousness," our Lord Jesus Christ, illumined the present day for the circle of the inhabited world; he rose through the cross; he saved the faithful through the cross. Let no one therefore be unbelieving toward the signs of the cross, but let him worship the blessed and thrice-blessed wood of the cross, and the signs of the cross by which the doors of heaven were opened for us. No longer "they light a lamp and put it under the bushel" — the bushel, I say, is the Law — "but upon the lampstand"; the lamp, moreover, is the Word. For under the Law the Word happened to be and was hidden to the unbelievers as under the bushel; but when he came upon the cross and was placed upon the lampstand, then he shone forth to the circle of the inhabited world.

lemmas.gloss: let us remain, stay by (hortatory subjunctive)
bushel, measuring basket (cover for a lamp)

choices.why: Glossary avoids 'morning star' which could imply Venus; 'dawn-bringer' fits the literal sense of bringing dawn and matches the rising light imagery.
Refers to physical festal torches carried in the night celebration; 'torches' is the plain term for δᾳδουχία.
Glossary locks 'bushel' for μόδιος as the vessel covering the lamp; it is the standard term in the lamp-under-bushel saying (Matt 5:15).
Glossary maps ὁ ἀόρατος πολέμιος to 'the invisible enemy' (the devil); 'invisible enemy' renders the phrase literally.
Standard literal rendering of ἀπαρχή; the congregation offers the first-fruits of Jesus' gifts.

bible_refs.note: Οὐκέτι καίουσι λύχνον καὶ ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον τιθέασιν ἀλλ᾽ ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν

pass_b_english: The heavens shine bright with the dancing of the stars, and all things gleam brighter still as the dawn-bringer rises. Yet this present night is not so much lit up by stars as it exults because our God and Savior has conquered. "Take courage," he says, "for I have conquered the world" (John 16:33). Since God has defeated the invisible enemy, we too shall rightly carry off the victory over demons. Let us stay by the saving cross, so that we may carry off the first-fruits of Jesus' gifts. Let us celebrate this holy night with holy torches, raising an inspired song and singing a heavenly hymn. The Sun of Righteousness, our Lord Jesus Christ, has illumined this present day for the whole circle of the inhabited world; he rose through the cross and rescued the faithful.

No one, then, should disbelieve the signs of the cross. Rather, let everyone worship the blessed and thrice-blessed wood of the cross, and the signs of the cross of him who opened the doors of heaven for us. They no longer "light a lamp and put it under a bushel" — by the bushel I mean the Law — "but on the lampstand," and by the lamp I mean the Word (Matthew 5:15). The Word happened to be under the Law and was hidden from unbelievers, just as a lamp is hidden under a bushel. But when he came upon the cross and was set upon the lampstand, then to the inhabited world.

problems.quote: and the signs of the cross that have opened the doors of heaven to us
problems.source_quote: τοῦ θύρας οὐρανοῦ ἡμῖν ἀνοί ξαντος
problems.why: The genitive participle ἀνοίξαντος refers to the one who opened heaven's doors, namely Christ. The English makes the signs the agent.
problems.fix: and the signs of him who opened the doors of heaven to us.

problems.quote: so that we may bring forward the first-fruits of Jesus' gifts
problems.source_quote: ἵνα τὰς πρώτας ἀπαρχὰς τῶν Ἰησοῦ δώρων ἀπενεγκώμεθα
problems.why: Middle ἀπενεγκώμεθα means to carry off or receive for ourselves the first-fruits of Jesus' gifts. 'Bring forward' suggests we offer them, which reverses the direction.
problems.fix: so that we may carry off the first-fruits of Jesus' gifts.

edits.new: and the signs of him who opened the doors of heaven to us

edits.old: so that we may bring forward the first-fruits of Jesus' gifts
edits.new: so that we may carry off the first-fruits of Jesus' gifts

fixed: Fixed agency: the genitive participle ἀνοίξαντος refers to Christ as the one who opened heaven's doors, not the signs. Changed 'signs ... that have opened' to 'signs of him who opened'.
Fixed direction: middle ἀπενεγκώμεθα means 'carry off/receive for ourselves', not 'bring forward/offer'. Changed to 'carry off the first-fruits of Jesus' gifts'.

problems.quote: They no longer "light a lamp and put it under a bushel" (Matthew 5:15). By the bushel I mean the Law, and by the lamp the Word.
problems.source_quote: «ἀλλ' ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν», λύχνον δὲ τὸν Λόγον
problems.why: The quoted antithesis “but on the lampstand,” which the gloss interrupts, is dropped, so the saying only forbids lighting a lamp.
problems.fix: They no longer “light a lamp and put it under a bushel”—by the bushel I mean the Law—“but on the lampstand,” and by the lamp I mean the Word (Matthew 5:15).
problems.ruling: Source has «ἀλλ' ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν» (but on the lampstand); English omits it, so the quote only forbids lighting a lamp, losing the antithesis.

fixed: Restored the dropped antithesis "but on the lampstand" from the Greek «ἀλλ' ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν» and reattached the identification of the lamp as the Word (λύχνον δὲ τὸν Λόγον), keeping the citation at the end.

problems.quote: and the signs of him who opened the doors of heaven to us
problems.source_quote: τοῖς τοῦ σταυροῦ συμβόλοις τοῦ θύρας οὐρανοῦ ἡμῖν ἀνοίξαντος
problems.why: The signs are signs of the cross; the participle names the one who opened heaven's doors.
problems.fix: and the signs of the cross of him who opened the doors of heaven for us.
problems.ruling: Source has τοῖς τοῦ σταυροῦ συμβόλοις ('signs of the cross'). English drops 'of the cross' and makes the signs belong to the one who opened heaven, changing the sense.

problems.quote: then he shone upon the whole inhabited world
problems.why: The Greek stops at a bare dative. 'Shone' and 'whole' are not in the source.
problems.ruling: Source breaks off at 'τότε τῷ τῆς οἰκουμένης', with no verb. 'He shone upon the whole inhabited world' is invented continuation, so the reader is misled about what the Greek says.

edits.old: and the signs of him who opened the doors of heaven to us
edits.new: and the signs of the cross of him who opened the doors of heaven for us

fixed: Fixed 'and the signs of him who opened the doors of heaven to us' -> 'and the signs of the cross of him who opened the doors of heaven for us' to match Greek 'τοῖς τοῦ σταυροῦ συμβόλοις τοῦ θύρας οὐρανοῦ ἡμῖν ἀνοίξαντος' (signs of the cross of the one who opened...).

Fixed 'then he shone upon the whole inhabited world.' -> 'then to the inhabited world.' because Greek 'τότε τῷ τῆς οἰκουμένης' is a bare dative with no verb 'shone' or 'whole'; the sentence breaks off at the dative.

last_rejected.quote: and the signs of the cross of him who opened the doors of heaven for us
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ τοῖς τοῦ σταυροῦ συμβόλοις τοῦ θύρας οὐρανοῦ ἡμῖν ἀνοίξαντος
last_rejected.why: The genitive participle states why the cross and its signs are worshipped; it does not make “of him who opened” a possessor of the signs.
last_rejected.fix: and the signs of the cross, for he has opened the doors of heaven for us.
last_rejected.ruling: τοῦ ... ἀνοίξαντος is genitive after τοῖς τοῦ σταυροῦ συμβόλοις; English 'signs of the cross of him who opened' is clumsy but conveys the same sense; the claim is a stylistic quibble.
